headline: Bruins drop a tough one to Winnipeg as the Garden goes silent
morning_brew: Wednesday night was an absolute disastah at the Garden. Watching the Bruins take a four to two loss to the Winnipeg Jets left me staring at the wall, just wondering how a game that started with that much energy ended up slipping through our fingers like a greased pig. Tanner Jeannot and Tyrel Bauer decided to turn the first period into a boxing match with that lengthy fight, and while I love the grit, it didn't do enough to spark the boys against a Jets team that kept finding the back of the net whenever we finally started to wake up.

Morgan Geekie and Fraser Minten managed to put points on the board, but we just couldn't sustain the pressure. Jeremy Swayman faced seventeen shots and came up short, and it's clear the defensive end needs to sharpen up before we host Toronto on Friday. I have been watching this team long enough to know when they are out of sync, and last night was a classic example of letting a winnable game turn into a frustrating two points for the visitors. Winnipeg just seemed to have an answer for every move we made, and watching that empty net goal in the final minutes was the final twist of the knife that ruined my damn night.

Looking ahead, the schedule doesn't get any easier with the Maple Leafs coming into town. We need a complete effort from the opening faceoff, or it's gonna be another long night for the faithful. I am hoping for a better showing because we've seen this group perform when they're locked in, and a Friday afternoon tilt is the perfect stage to wash the bad taste of this loss out of our mouths. I'll be in my seat, hoping the boys show the intensity we know they have, but honestly, I'm watching the next one through my fingers.
